It also shows potential inhalation and dermal/eye hazards, warranting an expanded perspective beyond formal GHS classifications (IHL and SKN Tier 2). However, comprehensive data is deficient for environmental, endocrine disruption, oral, and organ/systemic hazards, indicating significant gaps in its full hazard understanding in these areas.
Q2: Sodium metaborate dihydrate is not currently listed on any established "Lists of Concern." This absence may be partly due to the notable lack of comprehensive study, as reflected by its data-deficient status (Tier 4) in four out of seven hazard categories.
Q3: Despite having a well-defined molecular formula and substance class, sodium metaborate dihydrate appears to be insufficiently studied. With only 38 literature references—placing it at the 25th percentile of characterized chemicals—and four out of seven hazard categories classified as data deficient (Tier 4), its overall hazard profile remains largely incomplete.
